## Source
.design/m5/45-ml-classifier.md — decomposition PR 7.

## Surface
- New binary: `polaris-backend/src/bin/polaris_sample_classifier.rs` — rule-based fixture classifier that operators can run locally to exercise the integration.
- New docs: `docs/ops/classifier-integration.md` — how to register a classifier endpoint, configure trust weights, opt into feedback, set timeouts, monitor circuit-breaker state.

## Sample classifier rules
Trivially simple — its purpose is operator confidence, not production accuracy:
- Text containing `["spam", "win cash", "lottery"]` → `{label: "spam", confidence: 0.9}`
- Image blob_cid in a hard-coded "known bad" list → `{label: "graphic", confidence: 0.95}`
- Otherwise → no labels

## Rust-quality notes
- The sample binary is **deliberately simple** so its source is readable as documentation. Per rust-quality §9: keep it under 200 lines.
- Binary is a `tonic` server using the generated `polaris-classifier-proto` types (from #125). Pattern matches tonic's helloworld example.
- Per rust-quality §3 (binary crate): `anyhow::Result<()>` at the binary's entry; structured errors via `tracing::error!`.
- The docs file (`docs/ops/classifier-integration.md`) is markdown for operators. Each section has one runnable example. Per rust-quality §8: every CLI invocation in the doc is copy-pasteable and tested.
- The operator runbook explicitly addresses: (a) opt-in feedback, (b) self-vs-cloud privacy disclosure, (c) circuit-breaker observability, (d) trust-weight tuning. Each is a section heading.

## External references
- tonic server helloworld: https://github.com/hyperium/tonic/blob/master/examples/src/helloworld/server.rs
- v1 ops runbook (reference style): `docs/ops/runbook.md`

## Acceptance
- [ ] `cargo run --bin polaris_sample_classifier` starts a gRPC server on a configurable port.
- [ ] Pointing a polaris-backend at `localhost:<port>` materializes Observations as expected.
- [ ] `docs/ops/classifier-integration.md` exists; CI markdown-lint passes.
